IR.rationale: A rise in medium-term Treasury yields relative to the policy rate signals expected US tightening. That raises dollar funding costs and pulls capital out of emerging markets.

B.rationale: Strong EM sovereign bond returns alongside stable US corporate spreads indicate easy global credit and appetite for EM risk. Both support EM equity cash flows and valuations.

V.rationale: A high VIX reflects an elevated price of risk and a large variance risk premium. That state historically precedes higher subsequent returns on risky assets, including EM equities.

AP.rationale: US equities rallying while EM equities lag points to incomplete transmission of a global risk-on shock. Lead-lag effects suggest EM catches up.

ST.rationale: Weak momentum returns typically coincide with sharp rotations into beaten-down, high-beta assets. These are rebound phases in which EM equities tend to do well.

FX.rationale: A weakening dollar with a strengthening commodity currency marks global risk-on conditions. It also eases EM dollar-debt burdens, which supports EM equity returns.

COM.rationale: Rising broad commodity prices improve terms of trade and earnings for the many commodity-exporting EM economies.

MC.rationale: Tight financial conditions are associated with depressed prices and elevated risk premia. They therefore carry information about subsequent returns.

ENDG.rationale: EM equity indices show short-horizon return autocorrelation from slow information diffusion and investor flows.

IR.rationale: Abrupt repricing of expected US policy tightening triggers capital-flow reversals from EM and raises subsequent EM equity variance.

B.rationale: Widening credit spreads together with falling EM sovereign bond prices signal deteriorating credit conditions. Volatility in EM equities tends to rise after such shifts.

V.rationale: Jointly high equity and oil implied volatility marks broad cross-asset uncertainty. Option-implied variance carries forward-looking information beyond realised variance.

AP.rationale: Through the leverage and volatility-feedback effect, negative EM equity returns raise future volatility.

ST.rationale: High short-term reversal profits indicate scarce liquidity provision and disorderly price pressure. These conditions accompany elevated future volatility.

FX.rationale: Dollar strength combined with yen appreciation is the classic risk-off, carry-unwind configuration. It tends to precede turbulent EM markets.

COM.rationale: Falling oil prices strain commodity-exporting EM fiscal and external balances. This raises equity uncertainty.

MC.rationale: Elevated financial stress reflects funding strains and deleveraging. These conditions propagate to EM asset volatility.

ENDG.rationale: Volatility clustering means high recent realised variance carries information on future variance beyond the baseline.

IR.rationale: Sharp increases in expected US rates can trigger sudden stops in portfolio flows to EM. These are a key source of crash risk.

B.rationale: Widening spreads with selling in EM sovereign debt signal a credit-driven risk-off episode. Such episodes raise the probability of tail losses in EM equities.

V.rationale: High implied volatility widens the return distribution and signals crash-prone, fearful markets.

AP.rationale: Joint weakness in US and EM equities marks a global sell-off that tends to persist into further extreme losses.

ST.rationale: Momentum drawdowns coincide with stressed, high-volatility regimes in which tail outcomes are more likely.

FX.rationale: A surging dollar with a falling commodity currency tightens EM financial conditions. It accompanies capital flight.

COM.rationale: Commodity price slumps hit EM exporters' earnings and currencies. This raises the odds of large equity losses.

MC.rationale: Elevated financial stress indicates fragile funding markets in which forced deleveraging generates extreme losses.

ENDG.rationale: Poor recent EM returns signal a bearish, high-volatility regime in which further tail losses cluster.

IR.rationale: Falling short and medium-term US rates indicate monetary easing. That loosens global dollar liquidity and fuels EM rallies.

B.rationale: Rallying EM sovereign debt with stable US spreads reflects improving risk appetite. This favours strong EM equity gains.

V.rationale: High implied volatility widens both tails. Large rebounds tend to occur in high-volatility states after stress.

AP.rationale: Strong US equity returns transmit to EM with a lag through global risk appetite and flows.

ST.rationale: Momentum crashes occur when beaten-down high-beta assets rebound sharply. Such rebounds are typical of large EM gains.

FX.rationale: Dollar weakness combined with commodity-currency strength is a risk-on state that eases EM financing and attracts inflows.

COM.rationale: Commodity rallies boost EM exporters' terms of trade and earnings, raising the odds of large index gains.

MC.rationale: Tight financial conditions coincide with depressed valuations and high risk premia. From those levels, sharp relief rallies are more likely.

ENDG.rationale: Extreme gains tend to cluster in volatile regimes following weak returns, reflecting rebounds and mean reversion.
